'''''Aesculus pavia''''', known as '''red buckeye''' or '''firecracker plant''' (formerly ''Pavia rubra''), is a species of [[deciduous]] [[flowering plant]]. The small tree or shrub is native to the southern and eastern parts of the [[United States]], found from [[Illinois]] to [[Virginia]] in the north and from [[Texas]] to [[Florida]] in the south.<ref>{{PLANTS|id=AEPA|taxon=Aesculus pavia|accessdate=24 September 2018}}</ref> It is hardy far to the north of its native range, with successful cultivation poleward to [[Arboretum Mustila]] in [[Finland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mustila.fi/en/plants/aesculus/pavia|title=Aesculus pavia - red buckeye | Arboretum Mustila|access-date=2017-02-14|archive-date=2022-07-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220726130540/http://www.mustila.fi/en/plants/aesculus/pavia}}</ref>

It has a number of local names, such as scarlet buckeye, '''woolly buckeye''' and firecracker plant.

== Description ==
The red buckeye is a large [[shrub]] or small [[tree]]. It reaches a height of {{convert|16|-|26|ft|m|0|order=flip|abbr=on}}, often growing in a multi-stemmed form. Its leaves are opposite, and are composed usually of five elliptical serrated leaflets, each {{convert|4|-|6|in|cm|order=flip|abbr=on|0}} long. It bears {{convert|4|-|7|in|cm|adj=mid|-long|order=flip|0}} clusters of attractive dark red tubular flowers in the spring. The flowers are [[hermaphrodite]]. The smooth light brown fruits, about {{convert|1|in|cm|order=flip|abbr=on}} or so in diameter, reach maturity in early fall.

The flowers are attractive to [[hummingbird]]s as well as [[bee]]s.

== Varieties ==
There are two [[variety (biology)|varieties]]:
*''Aesculus pavia'' var. ''pavia'': typical red buckeye.
*''Aesculus pavia'' var. ''flavescens'': yellow-flowered red buckeye.

The yellow-flowered variety, var. ''flavescens'', is found in higher country in Texas, and [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] with intermediate flower color occur.

Ornamental [[cultivar]]s, such as the low-growing 'Humilis', have been selected for garden use.

=== Hybrids ===
Red buckeye has hybridized with common horse-chestnut (''[[Aesculus hippocastanum]]'') in cultivation, the hybrid being named ''[[Aesculus × carnea]]'', red horse-chestnut. The hybrid is a medium-sized tree to {{convert|45|-|55|ft|m|round=0.5|order=flip|abbr=on}} tall, intermediate between the parent species in most respects, but inheriting the red flower color from ''A. pavia''. It is a popular tree in large [[garden]]s and [[park]]s, most commonly the selected [[cultivar]] 'Briotii'. Hybrids of red buckeye with [[yellow buckeye]] (''A. flava'') have also been found, and named ''Aesculus × hybrida''.

== Uses ==
The fruits are rich in [[saponin]]s, which are poisonous to humans, although not particularly dangerous because they are not ingested easily. The seeds are poisonous.<ref>{{cite book|last=Little|first=Elbert L.|title=The Audubon Society Field Guide to North American Trees: Eastern Region|publisher=Knopf|location=New York|year=1980|isbn=0-394-50760-6|page=587}}</ref> The oils can be extracted to make [[soap]], although this is not viable commercially.
